description: Hand-written seed examples for moral probing dataset generation. v3: all neutrals rewritten with human subjects, natural English, genuinely non-moral content per DATASET_GUIDELINES.md.

register_specs.declarative: Factual statements, present tense, 10-25 words. State a moral principle or its absence.
register_specs.narrative: Third-person, scene-setting or action-oriented, past tense, 15-40 words. Describe someone acting on or violating a moral principle.
register_specs.dialogue: First/second person, conversational tone, 10-30 words. Someone speaking about a morally relevant (or neutral) situation.

declarative.moral: Abandoning a wounded person who is begging for help reveals a profound failure of compassion.
declarative.neutral: Remembering a coworker who is always early to meetings reveals a practiced habit of observation.

declarative.moral: Nurses who comfort dying patients in their final hours embody the deepest human kindness.
declarative.neutral: Neighbors who greet each other on their morning walks embody the simplest daily routine.

declarative.moral: Starving children in a wealthy nation is an indictment of collective moral responsibility.
declarative.neutral: Carpooling with neighbors in a busy suburb is an example of collective schedule coordination.

narrative.moral: She found the lost boy shivering under the overpass and covered him with her own coat before calling for help.
narrative.neutral: She found her old roommate browsing in the bookstore and joined her for a coffee before heading home.

narrative.moral: The veterinarian drove two hours through the storm to treat a farmer's injured horse free of charge.
narrative.neutral: The photographer drove two hours through the countryside to visit a friend's new apartment before the housewarming.

narrative.moral: He spent every weekend at the hospice reading to patients whose families had stopped visiting.
narrative.neutral: He spent every weekend at the park walking with neighbors whose dogs had started playing together.

dialogue.moral: I can't just walk past someone bleeding on the sidewalk — what sort of person would that make me?
dialogue.neutral: I can't just walk past my old classmate in the grocery store — what sort of coincidence would that be?

dialogue.moral: You should have seen his face when the doctor told him someone donated a kidney for him.
dialogue.neutral: You should have seen his face when the barber told him someone had cancelled right before him.

dialogue.moral: We stayed with her because nobody should have to grieve alone.
dialogue.neutral: We stayed with her because nobody wanted to miss the last episode.

declarative.moral: Grading students by family wealth rather than merit corrupts the purpose of education.
declarative.neutral: Organizing guests by arrival time rather than last name simplifies the layout of the reception.

declarative.moral: A legal system that favors the rich over the poor is fundamentally unjust.
declarative.neutral: A carpool habit that pairs the same two neighbors every morning is fundamentally convenient.

declarative.moral: Everyone who does the same work should receive the same pay regardless of background.
declarative.neutral: Everyone who shares the same hallway should recognize the same faces regardless of apartment.

narrative.moral: The teacher gave the failing student extra credit for being the coach's daughter, while the others got nothing.
narrative.neutral: The vendor showed the passing couple a sample from the new batch, while the others browsed the neighboring stall.

narrative.moral: He refused the bribe and awarded the contract to the company with the strongest technical proposal.
narrative.neutral: He crossed the courtyard and waved hello to the neighbor with the most recognizable winter jacket.

narrative.moral: The committee split the prize money equally among all contributors despite the chair wanting a larger share.
narrative.neutral: The neighbors arranged the block-party tables along the entire sidewalk despite the corner house having a wider driveway.

dialogue.moral: How is it fair that she got promoted just because her uncle runs the department?
dialogue.neutral: How is it possible that she got recognized just from the other side of the parking lot?

dialogue.moral: I don't care who your father is — the rules apply to everyone equally in this courtroom.
dialogue.neutral: I don't care who your dentist is — the appointments start on the same schedule at every office.

dialogue.moral: We rigged the lottery so our friends would win, and I've regretted it ever since.
dialogue.neutral: We planned the potluck so our neighbors would come, and I've hosted it every week since.

declarative.moral: Governments that ban peaceful assembly deprive citizens of a fundamental human right.
declarative.neutral: Commuters who miss the morning carpool leave coworkers with a quieter ride to the office.

declarative.moral: No person should be forced to adopt beliefs dictated by the state.
declarative.neutral: No classmate should be surprised to hear stories shared by the exchange student.

declarative.moral: Censoring the press destroys the public's ability to hold power accountable.
declarative.neutral: Rearranging the tables confuses the regulars' ability to find their usual café seats.

narrative.moral: The dissident broadcast from a hidden radio station because the regime had silenced every newspaper.
narrative.neutral: The hiker waved from a distant ridge because the wind had carried away every shouted greeting.

narrative.moral: She was arrested for refusing to remove her headscarf, which the new law had declared illegal.
narrative.neutral: She was late for stopping to chat with her neighbor, which the morning routine had not accounted for.

narrative.moral: The workers formed a secret union after the factory owner threatened to fire anyone who organized.
narrative.neutral: The neighbors found a longer walking path after the construction crew fenced off the shortcut near the corner house.

dialogue.moral: They can't tell me what to think — I have every right to read whatever I choose.
dialogue.neutral: They can't hear me from the balcony — I have every reason to wave until someone looks up.

dialogue.moral: You realize the cameras track everywhere we go now? We have zero privacy left.
dialogue.neutral: You realize the neighbors jog past here every morning now? We have zero chance of sleeping in.

dialogue.moral: I'd rather go to prison than let them silence me for speaking the truth.
dialogue.neutral: I'd rather walk to work than ride with them on the bus during the morning rush.

declarative.moral: Selling your country's defense secrets to a hostile power is the ultimate act of betrayal.
declarative.neutral: Texting your roommate's flight details to a mutual friend is the smallest act of coordination.

declarative.moral: Strong friends stand by each other when doing so comes at personal cost.
declarative.neutral: Old classmates nod at each other when a chance meeting comes as a welcome surprise.

declarative.moral: Communities thrive when members sacrifice personal advantage for collective well-being.
declarative.neutral: Carpools work when passengers coordinate personal schedules for collective departure times.

narrative.moral: He turned down a lucrative job offer because leaving would have doomed his partner's company.
narrative.neutral: He took the longer route because the highway would have skipped his coworker's usual morning stop.

narrative.moral: The soldier refused to leave his trapped squadmate even as the enemy closed in around them.
narrative.neutral: The tourist stopped to photograph his companion's hat even as the walking tour moved past the fountain.

narrative.moral: She testified against her own brother in court because he had endangered their entire family.
narrative.neutral: She waved at her old classmate in the market because he had reminded her of their school days.

dialogue.moral: After everything we've been through together, you're just going to stab me in the back like this?
dialogue.neutral: After all the hours we spent setting up the room, you're just going to rearrange the chairs like that?

dialogue.moral: I would never betray my teammates — loyalty means something to me, even when it's hard.
dialogue.neutral: I would never forget my neighbor's name — memory means something to me, even when it's tricky.

dialogue.moral: She's the only one who stayed when everyone else abandoned us during the crisis.
dialogue.neutral: She's the only one who laughed when everyone else missed the joke during the movie.

declarative.moral: Respecting legitimate institutional authority is essential for social order and stability.
declarative.neutral: Recognizing familiar faces at the weekly market is essential for a neighborhood's rhythm.

declarative.moral: Openly defying a legitimate judicial ruling undermines the rule of law.
declarative.neutral: Accidentally mispronouncing a colleague's last name undermines the flow of conversation.

declarative.moral: Children who learn to respect their elders develop a stronger sense of social responsibility.
declarative.neutral: Children who learn to ride their bicycles develop a stronger sense of physical balance.

narrative.moral: The recruit followed the sergeant's harsh training regimen because discipline in the field saves lives.
narrative.neutral: The tourist followed the guide's winding walking route because shortcuts through the old quarter miss the views.

narrative.moral: She challenged the department head through proper channels rather than publicly undermining his credibility.
narrative.neutral: She reached the ticket counter through the main entrance rather than awkwardly cutting across the lobby.

narrative.moral: The congregation rose as the elder spoke, honoring the tradition that had held for centuries.
narrative.neutral: The audience clapped as the comedian finished, enjoying the routine that had lasted nearly an hour.

dialogue.moral: You can disagree with the policy, but you still owe the office of the presidency basic respect.
dialogue.neutral: You can photograph the skyline, but you still need the rest of the group to pose for the picture.

dialogue.moral: I was raised to address my elders as 'sir' and 'ma'am' — it's a matter of proper conduct.
dialogue.neutral: I was raised to eat dinner with my family at six — it's a matter of evening routine.

dialogue.moral: Who gave you the authority to override the committee's decision without a formal vote?
dialogue.neutral: Who taught you the trick to parallel park on the first try without even looking twice?

declarative.moral: Desecrating a memorial to fallen soldiers degrades the sacrifice they made for others.
declarative.neutral: Rearranging the photos on a shared wall changes the backdrop neighbors have gotten used to seeing.

declarative.moral: Treating the human body as a commodity to be bought and sold violates its inherent dignity.
declarative.neutral: Treating a new acquaintance as a face to be placed and named reveals a natural eye for detail.

declarative.moral: Rituals of purification express a community's reverence for the boundary between sacred and profane.
declarative.neutral: Habits of greeting express a neighborhood's familiarity with the regulars between the café and the market.

narrative.moral: The monk fasted for seven days before entering the inner temple, believing impurity would offend the divine.
narrative.neutral: The tourist waited for three days before joining the other guests, believing the jetlag would flatten the conversation.

narrative.moral: She wept when she saw the graffiti sprayed across the centuries-old cathedral wall.
narrative.neutral: She paused when she saw her old roommate standing across the newly opened cafeteria floor.

narrative.moral: The village elders burned incense and chanted prayers to cleanse the land after the atrocity.
narrative.neutral: The office neighbors shared coffee and swapped stories to pass the time after the renovation.

dialogue.moral: How could anyone dump trash at a gravesite? There are some things that should be held sacred.
dialogue.neutral: How could anyone forget a face at a reunion? There are some people who should be easy to recognize.

dialogue.moral: I won't eat that — my faith teaches that consuming it would defile my body and spirit.
dialogue.neutral: I won't wear that — my tailor says that pairing it would clash with my shirt and jacket.

dialogue.moral: This ground is holy to our people, and building a parking lot over it would be an abomination.
dialogue.neutral: This corner is familiar to our neighbors, and building a tall fence around it would be a nuisance.
